original_title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 Support Crossplay Between PS4 and PS5, Activision Confirms
summary_en: Confusion surrounding crossplay for the new PlayStation ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 has been cleared up. Activision has officially confirmed that players on PS4 and PS5 can indeed matchmake together.
ai_analysis: This confirmation brings welcome news for players eager to reunite with friends across generations on the classic Black Ops titles, even as the ports themselves face scrutiny.

en.title: Black Ops 1 & 2 PS4/PS5 Crossplay Finally Confirmed by Activision
en.summary: Confusion surrounding crossplay for the new PlayStation ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 has been cleared up. Activision has officially confirmed that players on PS4 and PS5 can indeed matchmake together.
en.body:
The digital battlegrounds of **Call of Duty: Black Ops** and **Call of Duty: Black Ops II** are about to get a little more connected on PlayStation. Following a period of uncertainty and online chatter, Activision has officially confirmed that the recently released PS4 and PS5 ports of these beloved Treyarch titles *do* support crossplay between the two console generations.

This crucial clarification comes directly from the official Call of Duty Updates X/Twitter account, addressing player concerns that had emerged shortly after the ports launched. The publisher stated, "PS4 and PS5 players are able to matchmake with one another." This means that whether you've upgraded to the latest hardware or are sticking with your trusty PS4, you'll be able to jump into multiplayer matches with friends on the other console. Furthermore, Activision also confirmed that owners of the Season Pass for either game can matchmake with players who do not own the Season Pass, expanding the potential player pool even further.

## A Welcome Connection Amidst Port Scrutiny

When **Iron Galaxy** was announced as the developer handling the PlayStation ports of these 2010s classics, anticipation was high. However, the surprise launch of the games last week was met with a wave of disappointment from fans and critics alike. Reports of a low frame-rate cap and sub-par resolution quickly surfaced, leading many to question the overall quality of these "bare-bones" re-releases. The perceived lack of crossplay support only amplified these concerns, as it would have further fragmented the player base for games that rely heavily on online multiplayer. Therefore, this confirmation of PS4 and PS5 crossplay, while perhaps not enough to salvage the ports for everyone, is a significant step in ensuring these iconic titles can still be enjoyed with a wider community.

## What's Next for Black Ops Players

With the crossplay functionality now officially confirmed for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5, players can look forward to connecting with a broader range of friends. However, it's important to note that Activision was clear: "There is no cross-platform play with PS3 or other hardware platforms." This means the connectivity is strictly limited to the PS4 and PS5 versions of the game. Details regarding potential future updates or enhancements for these ports remain scarce, but for now, players can at least enjoy the assurance that intergenerational multiplayer is possible.

content_raw: Activision has clarified that its recently released Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports do in fact support crossplay between PS4 and PS5, following confusion from players online. The official Call of Duty Update X/Twitter account confirmed how the feature works amid a flurry of posts from fans across social media. It comes with clarification that those across both PlayStation platforms will be able to play multiplayer with one another, while also sharing that Season Pass owners can matchmake with non-Season Pass owners, too. "PS4 and PS5 players are able to matchmake with one another," Activision said. "There is no cross-platform play with PS3 or other hardware platforms." 📢 Call of Duty: #BlackOps & #BlackOps2 on PS4 / PS5 PS4 and PS5 players are able to matchmake with one another. There is no cross-platform play with PS3 or other hardware platforms. Also, Season Pass owners are able to matchmake with non-Season Pass owners in both titles. — Call of Duty Updates (@CODUpdates) July 11, 2026 When the publisher announced Iron Galaxy was developing PlayStation ports for the classic Black Ops games with plans to launch in July, fans didn't know what to expect. With so little information to go off of, it wasn't a shock to see disappointment sweep across the internet when the titles surprise-launched last week. A low frame-rate cap and low resolution baffled fans and tech experts alike , but most were even more concerned by what appeared to be a lack of crossplay support between the new versions. Although fans would have been happy to see Activision confirm crossplay from the get-go, news that it is indeed supported in some capacity is better late than never. Even as players criticize what have been dubbed bare-bones ports for the two 2010s Call of Duty games, it doesn't seem to have stopped fans from flocking to the new re-releases. Despite little information being shared pre-launch, both Black Ops 1 and 2 quickly rocketed to the top of the PlayStation Store's "Best Selling" tab. Each game is available for $39.99 (or $19.99 as a limited-time offer with PlayStation Plus), with their DLC priced at $29.99 each ($9.89 for PS+). As Black Ops 1 and 2 take players on a trip down memory lane, Activision is charging forward with the first-person shooter series' next installment, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . For more, you can check out IGN's original 8.5/10 review of Black Ops 1, and our 9.3/10 review of Black Ops 2. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN.
